George Russell is hopeful Mercedes' long-awaited car upgrade at the Bahrain Grand Prix will further help his performances as he bids to build on his return to winning ways from Azerbaijan last week. Russell dominated the Baku event to not only secure his first win in seven races but also claim the maiden 'Grand Slam' of his Formula 1 career, meaning he led every lap from pole position and set the fastest lap. The Briton had been happier with his performances in Mercedes' W17 since the August summer break, yet he had still finished behind title-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli in each of the previous three races, with Antonelli extending his championship advantage to 81 points after victory in Madrid. messages.text: Former Wallaby hooker Charles confirms MND diagnosis

metadata.summary: Former Australia rugby international Nathan Charles, who overcame cystic fibrosis to forge a professional career in a contact sport, has been diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND).
metadata.content: Nathan Charles: Former Australia rugby international reveals motor neurone disease diagnosis | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nathan Charles: Former Australia rugby international reveals motor neurone disease diagnosis Nathan Charles has revealed his motor neurone disease (MND) diagnosis; the 37-year-old made four appearances for Australia across 2014 and 2015; Charles overcame cystic fibrosis to produce a decorated career in professional rugby Thursday 1 October 2026 08:23, UK Image: Nathan Charles made four appearances for Australia across 2014 and 2015 Former Australia rugby international Nathan Charles, who overcame cystic fibrosis to forge a professional career in a contact sport, has been diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND). The 37-year-old Charles, who made his Test debut in 2014 and earned four caps for the Wallabies, including a 12-12 draw against New Zealand, revealed he has been diagnosed with the same illness as recently retired National Rugby League star Jai Arrow. MND is an umbrella term for a group of progressive neurological conditions where the motor neurones degenerate. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is the most common form, and ALS is often called Lou Gehrig's disease. During an interview with former Wallabies lock and now commentator Justin Harrison on Stan Sport this week, Charles revealed he had only recently been diagnosed. messages.text: Toney pleads not guilty to assault charge

metadata.summary: England forward Ivan Toney appeared in a London court on Thursday to plead not guilty to a charge of assault causing actual bodily harm over an incident at a nightclub in central London last December.
metadata.content: Ivan Toney: England forward pleads not guilty to assault charge in court following nightclub incident | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ivan Toney: England forward pleads not guilty to assault charge in court following nightclub incident Ivan Toney was originally charged on July 31 and is accused of attacking a man at a nightclub in central London last December; the England forward denies the charges Thursday 1 October 2026 14:11, UK Image: Ivan Toney pleaded not guilty to a charge of assault in court England forward Ivan Toney appeared in a London court on Thursday to plead not guilty to a charge of assault causing actual bodily harm over an incident at a nightclub in central London last December. Toney stood in the dock at Westminster Magistrates' Court to confirm his name and age, and issue his not guilty plea to an incicient that happended on December 6 at a Soho club, where he is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva. The 30-year-old, wearing a black top over a shirt and tie, was accompanied by three members of his entourage as he arrived at court shortly after 9.30am. The criminal case came after an investigation by London's Metropolitan Police and the charge was announced in late July. In a statement, his spokesperson said: "Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court."
